newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share volumes plunge 59 pct in Q3 1996.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share volumes plunge 59 pct in Q3 1996.

text.p: The number of shares traded on the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) plunged 59 percent year-on-year in the third quarter of 1996 to 5.7 billion, the Straits Times newspaper said on Wednesday.
The quarter's share tally was worth a total of Singapore $15.5 billion, down 41 percent, the newspaper said.

In September, share volumes were down almost 61 percent year-on-year to 1.8 billion, the second consecutive month in which liquidity had shrunk to less than half the volume traded over the same period a year ago, it said.
The total value of shares traded in September was down 36 percent to around Singapore $5.00 billion.

The figures were compiled by the newspaper from daily totals of trades on the SES main board, secondary SESDAQ and over-the-counter Clob International boards. They exclude non-Singapore dollar shares.

Dealers blame the poor liquidity on a prolonged fall in share prices which pulled Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) down to around 2,080 points in July from a high of just over 2,500 points in early February.
Since then, the index has mostly kept within a narrow trading range between 2,100 and 2,200 points.
Dealers said overseas demand for Singapore shares had also been depressed by a recent down-weighting of Singapore in the influential Morgan Stanley Far East ex-Japan stock index.
Analysts say the low stockmarket volumes threaten to depress earnings for banks and finance houses with broking arms.
